description.summary: permission to expose an app's UI to AI agents

protocol.description:
This protocol lets an application ask for permission to expose its user interface to AI agents, for instance through an MCP server that lets an agent read the app's accessibility tree and act on it. Exposing a UI to an agent hands it everything the user sees and can do in the app, so the decision belongs to the user, and the compositor is the party that can ask them in a way the application cannot spoof.
The application describes itself and why it wants access. The compositor decides, by policy or by asking the user, and answers with a grant carrying an opaque token, or a denial. A grant lasts until the application destroys the object or the compositor revokes it. The token is what the application presents to the agent bridge; a bridge only serves apps whose token the compositor vouches for.
Only privileged clients can bind the manager global. A compositor must not expose it to sandboxed clients.
Warning! The protocol described in this file is currently in the testing phase. Backward compatible changes may be added together with the corresponding interface version bump. Backward incompatible changes can only be done by creating a new major version of the extension.

interface.name: crownos_agent_access_manager_v1
interface.description: A global factory for crownos_agent_access_v1 objects.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroy the manager. Requests made through it are unaffected.

request.name: request_access
request.description:
Ask for permission to expose the application's UI to AI agents. The compositor answers on the new object with granted or denied, possibly much later if it asks the user.
app_id identifies the application to the user and should match the app_id of the application's toplevels. A request with an empty app_id is denied, since the user could not be told who is asking. reason is a short, human-readable explanation the compositor may show the user when asking, and may be empty.

interface.name: crownos_agent_access_v1
interface.description: The outcome of one request_access. Exactly one of granted or denied is sent first; revoked may follow granted. After denied or revoked no further events are sent and the object should be destroyed.

request.name: destroy

description.summary: give up the request or the grant

request.description: Destroy the object. A pending request is withdrawn and a grant ends: its token is no longer valid.

event.name: granted
event.description: The application may expose its UI to agents. token is an opaque string identifying this grant, valid until the object is destroyed or revoked is sent. Clients must not interpret it.

event.name: denied
event.description: The application must not expose its UI to agents. This is the last event sent on the object.

event.name: revoked
event.description: The grant ended, for example because the user withdrew it. The token is no longer valid and the application must stop exposing its UI to agents. This is the last event sent on the object.
